title: Helena Pharma renewal + EU private pilot check-in
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a renewal + expansion check-in with Helena Pharma to confirm EU private pilot scope, discuss capacity uplift numbers, and align on security docs and timeline. Customer still evaluating dedicated vs hosted for some workloads; priority is EU data residency and KMS/HSM integration. Action items assigned for a bench run and a revised quote. Next step: pilot kickoff pending security review and signed amendment.
next_steps: Sofia: send revised 12-month renewal + pilot pricing by 2026-02-09
Liam: deliver latency and throughput bench (p50/p95, 8k seq, 1k concurrency) by 2026-02-11
Marta: share list of compliance contacts and SOC2 sub-scope by 2026-02-10
action_items: Sofia Patel: Revised quote and amendment draft (due 2026-02-09)
Liam Chen: Run private pilot perf bench on EU cluster; share raw logs and p95 numbers (due 2026-02-11)
Marta Klein: Provide contact for internal auditor + SOC2 checklist (due 2026-02-10)
Grace Mendoza: Confirm which workloads must remain in private VPC vs can use hosted (due 2026-02-12)
meeting_header: 2026-02-06 15:00 UTC | 48 minutes | Helena Pharma renewal & EU private pilot check-in
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you making time. uh quick roll call — i'm sofia from Redwood, liam is on the call to cover the perf details.
[00:12] Grace Mendoza: hi sofia, hi liam, grace here. arjun and marta are with me. thanks.
[00:18] Arjun Rao: hey team, yep quick intro from my side. big thing for us is residency and also the contract term.
[00:25] Liam Chen: great — i'll, i'll flag up front i'll go through the bench plan and the staging topology, then we can talk numbers.
[00:33] Sofia Patel: perfect. so agenda, re-iterate renewal options, confirm EU private pilot scope and timeline, and then liam's bench details + security asks.
[00:44] Grace: sounds good. we ran your hosted instance for three months, production traffic is around 4M tokens/day, spiking to about 8M on peak. our ask is to secure an additional dedicated pool for EU to meet p95 latency < 180ms for typical 2k seq requests.
[01:05] Liam: okay that's helpful, does that 4M include embeddings calls? or is it purely generation?
[01:11] Grace: mostly generation, embeddings are small fraction. we do some heavy reranking during batch jobs overnight.
[01:18] Sofia: great. on the renewal, the standard path is a 12-month extension with a committed dedicated pool; we can structure pilot as a 60-day private VPC pilot that transitions into dedicated capacity if it meets SLOs.
[01:32] Marta Klein: quick interjection — from security side we need KMS integration and proof of HSM-backed key wrapping for EU region. also SOC2 in-scope evidence and SAML SSO.
[01:46] Sofia: absolutely — we can include KMS + bring-your-own-key in the pilot scope. i'll attach the SOC2 bridging docs; note that some of the nomenclature in the doc can be noisy, happy to walk through.
[01:58] Arjun: for the dedicated pool, what's the lead time to provision EU GPUs and do you support private HA across two AZs? we've seen provisioning waits elsewhere.
[02:08] Liam: typical lead time is 2-3 weeks once the amendment is signed and payment clears. for EU we can provision across two availability zones in the region for failover — for private deployments we do VPC peering or customer-managed transit, depends on your networking team preference.
[02:25] Grace: okay 2-3 weeks is fine. the more pressing is the perf — can you confirm token-level cost and expected p50/p95 numbers — we need to compare against an internal onprem runtime.
[02:38] Liam: yeah, so for the model variant you ran (we think it was the 13B-ish open model), typical p50 is ~80ms on an a100 equivalent with continuous batching; p95 is around 210ms for long sequences, but with the EU dedicated pool and the quantization profile we recommended we expect to get p95 down to under 180ms. caveat: those numbers vary with concurrency and sequence-length distribution.
[03:05] Grace: the sequence distribution will be a mix — 60% sub-512 tokens, 30% 512-2k, 10% long 8k-ish for document synthesis.
[03:16] Sofia: understood. liam, maybe mention the KV cache/ prefix caching — we can save a lot there for multi-turn vs single-shot.
[03:23] Liam: yes, our prefix caching will cut repeated context retrieval; for your mix we estimate ~15-20% token cost reduction with caching + batching. also we recommend enabling automatic batching window of 15ms for interactive endpoints; that'll improve throughput.
[03:40] Arjun: and what about fallbacks? if dedicated pool gets saturated can requests go to hosted EU region temporarily?
[03:48] Sofia: we can set up a routing policy — primary to dedicated EU pool, fallback to hosted compatible model in EU region with rate limits. that adds a slight variance in latency but keeps availability.
[03:58] Marta: on the compliance front, we will need audit logs retained for 7 years and signed attestations for data deletion. do you support extended log retention and export to our SIEM?
[04:10] Sofia: yes, we have log export to customer-managed S3 or syslog; retention tiers can be extended as an add-on. we'll note retention 7 years as part of the pilot SOW.
[04:22] Grace: great. pricing — we saw the preliminary renewal numbers you shared, but we need a clear committed vs burst chart. for budgeting we want a committed baseline and then burst pricing that caps monthly cost.
[04:34] Sofia: sure — the revised quote will include a committed baseline (N GPU-hours equivalent) and a burst bucket at discounted rates; i'll include a sample pro-forma with spend caps.
[04:44] Liam: i'll also include recommended quantization variants — 4-bit vs 8-bit tradeoffs — because that impacts both cost and latency. 4-bit gives ~35% cost reduction but longer compile time and slightly lower quality for certain tasks.
[04:59] Arjun: hm we need to run an eval against our prompt set, we care about hallucination and factuality regressions more than micro latency. can you support eval harness for the pilot?
[05:09] Liam: yes, we can run a seeded eval with your prompt set during the pilot; we'll instrument quality metrics and regression alerts tied to the eval suite.
[05:20] Grace: good. can you also provide an SLA variant for private pilot? we need a baseline uptime commitment and credits for infra failures.
[05:29] Sofia: for pilot we provide non-SLA but with operational playbooks; when you convert to dedicated we can add SLA (up to 99.95) in the amendment.
[05:39] Marta: one last question: does Redwood allow customer-managed KMS with HSM (bring-your-own-key) on private deployments? we can't have keys in Redwood-managed KMS.
[05:49] Liam: yes, we support BYOK via KMS connect and HSM integration; for private deployments keys never leave your HSM and we operate with wrapped keys. we'll need the KMS endpoint and certificate exchange during onboarding.
[06:01] Grace: noted. okay — timeline for pilot kickoff? we'd like to start in late feb if possible.
[06:07] Sofia: target week of 2026-02-22 sounds achievable. i'll send the amendment and revised quote by 2026-02-09 so legal can review.
[06:14] Arjun: okay please include a clause for a 30-day exit if the pilot doesn't meet SLOs; legal insisted on an escape clause.
[06:22] Sofia: we can include a pilot exit clause.
[06:25] Grace: perfect.
[06:27] Liam: i'll outline the bench plan now — step one: we'll provision an EU private cluster with the same model + quantization profile; step two: synthetic throughput runs to validate concurrency targets; step three: replay a subset of production traffic for 48 hours to measure p95 under realistic load; step four: run eval suite for hallucination/factuality. deliverables: p50/p95 graphs, token cost estimates, and a canary rollout plan.
[06:53] Arjun: replaying production traffic — how do you handle PII? we can't send raw data off, obfuscation?
[07:00] Liam: we can run the replay inside the private VPC so data never leaves your network; if you prefer, we can also provide an anonymized synthetic replay.
[07:09] Grace: we'll do private VPC replay.
[07:12] Sofia: good. i'm going to summarize action items now.
[07:16] Sofia: action items — i will send revised quote and amendment; liam will run bench and share p95 numbers; marta to share SOC2 contact and KMS endpoint; grace to confirm which routes must be private. target pilot week 2026-02-22.
[07:31] Grace: sounds right. one minor thing — competitor pricing: we're also talking to Anthropic about a similar private pilot; price/perf looks close.
[07:40] Sofia: understood, we'll be competitive and will show the regression + perf delta during the bench.
[07:45] Arjun: any concerns about switching models mid-pilot? we sometimes need to change to a smaller model for cost control mid-run.
[07:53] Liam: that's supported — we can route traffic between model variants and do canary rollouts. there is a config change when switching quantization but rollout can be automated.
[08:03] Marta: okay from security side as long as we get the certificate exchange and KMS proof-of-concept before data replays.
[08:11] Sofia: absolutely. i'll coordinate with your security team.
[08:15] Grace: great, i think that's everything. thanks all.
[08:18] Sofia: thanks everyone — recap and next steps: quote by 2/9, bench by 2/11, security contacts by 2/10, target kickoff week of 2/22. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[08:33] Arjun: thanks.
[08:35] Marta: thanks.
[08:37] meeting ended
